statement: The minimum number of real common tangent lines to two circles in R^2 is zero.

source.location: Elementary strict-containment deduction; finite generic affine problem: Introduction and Theorem 2(a), printed pp.1–2

scope: Unrestricted positive-radius Euclidean spheres, with regular generic finite complex tangent fibre; no equal-radius or pairwise-disjoint-ball restriction.
notes: Put one closed ball strictly inside another, with centre distance strictly less than the difference of the radii. A line tangent to the inner sphere enters the interior of the outer ball and therefore cannot be tangent to the outer sphere. Strict containment persists under small perturbation; choosing a generic configuration in this open set gives a regular fibre with no real common tangent. This elementary deduction does not apply to the equal-radius subfamily used in all-real constructions. For n=2 the same proof is about the existing two-circle instance; the 3·2^(n−1) degree formula is not applied there.
